The Feasts of the Most High

precepts.text: The officers of the children of Israel, which Pharaoh's taskmasters had set over them, were beaten. The taskmasters set officers of our own people over us. In America those are called house negroes; in ancient Egypt they were called officers. Some of them had a good living, until the beatings came to them too.
precepts.point: Some of our people in ancient Egypt had money and high standing, and they were okay with the oppression they were living under. It is the same thing today: the celebrities, the entertainers, the pastors with money that are comfortable here in modern day Egypt. When a people live in oppression for centuries, oppression becomes a norm; you watch at it as a way of life. That is why the scripture talks about us trusting in the shadow of Egypt, trusting in oppression.

note.label: Passover Class: Exodus From America Modern Day Egypt

precepts.why:
Moses “refused to be called the son of Pharaoh’s daughter; Choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of God”. Understand that in ancient Egypt everybody was not bad off. Things were not bad for Moses; Moses made things bad for himself by killing the Egyptian, and there was a consequence for killing an Egyptian, so Moses was on the run.

Exodus 5:14 shows that some of our own people were set up over us: “And the officers of the children of Israel, which Pharaoh’s taskmasters had set over them, were beaten, and demanded, Wherefore have ye not fulfilled your task in making brick both yesterday and to day, as heretofore?” The taskmasters set officers of the children of Israel over us. In ancient Egypt they were called officers; in America they are called Uncle Tom Negroes, house Negroes.

To be an officer you were making money. Some of our people in ancient Egypt had money and high standing, a form of good living, and they were okay with the oppression they were going through, until the officers started getting their behinds whooped too.

It is the same thing today: Beyoncé, Usher, the pastor praying for Trump, people with money who are comfortable here in modern day Egypt, spiritual Egypt. When a people live in oppression for centuries, oppression becomes a norm and you take it as a way of life. That is why the scripture talks about us trusting in the shadow of Egypt, trusting in oppression. Moses had that comfort and refused it, choosing to suffer affliction with the people of God.

precepts.text: Consider the Apostle and High Priest of our profession, Christ Jesus; the work of the Lord is the profession of the called.
precepts.point: The work of the Lord is the true calling over any occupation held in Babylon: consider the Apostle and High Priest of our profession, Christ Jesus; fight the good fight of faith, lay hold on eternal life, whereunto thou art also called, and hast professed a good profession before many witnesses.
precepts.why:
Pharaoh said, “Let there more work be laid upon the men, that they may labour therein; and let them not regard vain words.” The same tactic runs in this captivity: burdens are increased and extra wages dangled for working the Sabbath and the feast days, to wear the people down so they will not regard the words of the Most High.

“Wherefore, holy brethren, partakers of the heavenly calling, consider the Apostle and High Priest of our profession, Christ Jesus”. The work of the Lord is the profession of the called, the true calling over any occupation held in Babylon. Pharaoh called Israel idle for wanting to go and sacrifice to their God; the words he called vain are the calling.

precepts.text: Fight the good fight of faith, lay hold on eternal life, whereunto thou art also called, and hast professed a good profession before many witnesses.
precepts.point: The work of the Lord is the true calling over any occupation held in Babylon: consider the Apostle and High Priest of our profession, Christ Jesus; fight the good fight of faith, lay hold on eternal life, whereunto thou art also called, and hast professed a good profession before many witnesses.
precepts.why:
“Fight the good fight of faith, lay hold on eternal life, whereunto thou art also called, and hast professed a good profession before many witnesses.”

Pharaoh laid more work upon the men so that they would not regard vain words, and this captivity does the same, dangling extra wages for working the Sabbath and the feast days. The good profession, professed before many witnesses, is the work of the Lord, the true calling over any occupation held in Babylon; fight the good fight of faith and lay hold on eternal life rather than the taskmaster's wages.

precepts.text: The great city, which spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt, where also our Lord was crucified.
precepts.point: This place is the same house of bondage in the spirit: the great city is spiritually called Sodom and Egypt, and the afflictions Egypt laid on Israel are the same tactics laid on Israel here.
precepts.why:
“And their dead bodies shall lie in the street of the great city, which spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt, where also our Lord was crucified.”

This place is the same house of bondage in the spirit. The afflictions Egypt laid on Israel are the same tactics laid on Israel here: fewer resources, the same production and the same deadline, stubble instead of straw and “Fulfil your works, your daily tasks, as when there was straw.” And the officers of the children of Israel, set over their own people by Pharaoh's taskmasters, were beaten, so that the anger of the oppressed lands on their own brother, the supervisor they can see, instead of on the power above him. It has always been an agenda, and in the great city spiritually called Egypt it is the same one today.

precepts.text: The chief priests and Pharisees said, If we let him thus alone, the Romans shall come and take away both our place and nation; men set over the people fear losing their place more than they love the deliverer.
precepts.point: The officers did see that they were in evil case. That is when they realized no appeal to Pharaoh would deliver them; deliverance was not coming from Egypt.
precepts.why:
The officers of the children of Israel cried unto Pharaoh, and his answer was, “Ye are idle, ye are idle: therefore ye say, Let us go and do sacrifice to the Lord.” The charge of idleness is the standing answer to any who would go serve God, whether it is the three days' journey or keeping the Sabbath and the new moons now.

The chief priests and the Pharisees gathered a council and said, “If we let him thus alone, all men will believe on him: and the Romans shall come and take away both our place and nation.” Men set over the people fear losing their place more than they love the deliverer. The officers did see that they were in evil case: no appeal to Pharaoh would deliver them, and deliverance was not coming from Egypt.

precepts.text: Moses and Aaron told Pharaoh, Let my people go, that they may hold a feast unto me in the wilderness; this is what the Most High says to Esau, who hardens his heart like Pharaoh.
precepts.point: Oh that the salvation of Israel were come out of Zion! When God bringeth back the captivity of his people, Jacob shall rejoice and Israel shall be glad. We long to serve the Most High without fear, free of the pressures of Christmas and birthdays at work.

note.label: Psalm 53: The Fool Says There Is No God

precepts.why:
“And afterward Moses and Aaron went in, and told Pharaoh, Thus saith the Lord God of Israel, Let my people go, that they may hold a feast unto me in the wilderness.” This is what the Most High says to Esau, who hardens his heart like Pharaoh. Let my people go, that they may serve him and keep his feasts without fear.

When God bringeth back the captivity of his people, it is the same word Moses brought to Pharaoh. Jacob shall rejoice and Israel shall be glad.

points: Moses and Aaron went in and told Pharaoh, Thus saith the LORD God of Israel, Let my people go, that they may hold a feast unto me in the wilderness. That feast was the Passover.
Pharaoh said, Who is the LORD, that I should obey his voice to let Israel go? I know not the LORD, neither will I let Israel go. The Lord had already said He would harden Pharaoh's heart.

They said, The God of the Hebrews hath met with us: let us go, we pray thee, three days' journey into the desert, and sacrifice unto the LORD our God; lest he fall upon us with pestilence, or with the sword.

The king of Egypt said, Wherefore do ye, Moses and Aaron, let the people from their works? get you unto your burdens. That is the standing complaint of the oppressor: the prophets are pulling the people from their labor and getting their hopes up that their God will deliver them.

Pharaoh commanded the taskmasters the same day: ye shall no more give the people straw to make brick; let them go and gather straw for themselves; and the tale of the bricks ye shall lay upon them, ye shall not diminish ought thereof. For they be idle; therefore they cry, saying, Let us go and sacrifice to our God.

Let there more work be laid upon the men, that they may labour therein; and let them not regard vain words. The same tactic runs in this captivity: burdens are increased and extra wages dangled for working the Sabbath and the feast days, to wear the people down so they will not regard the words of the Most High.

The people were scattered abroad throughout all the land of Egypt to gather stubble instead of straw, and the taskmasters hasted them, saying, Fulfil your works, your daily tasks, as when there was straw. Fewer resources, the same production and the same deadline: the pattern of oppression has not changed in this captivity.

The officers of the children of Israel, which Pharaoh's taskmasters had set over them, were beaten. Israelites were set as officers over their own people, so that the anger of the oppressed lands on their own brother, the supervisor they can see, instead of on the power above him; it has always been an agenda, and it is the same one today.

The officers of the children of Israel came and cried unto Pharaoh, saying, Wherefore dealest thou thus with thy servants? There is no straw given unto thy servants, and they say to us, Make brick: and, behold, thy servants are beaten; but the fault is in thine own people.

Pharaoh answered, Ye are idle, ye are idle: therefore ye say, Let us go and do sacrifice to the LORD. The charge of idleness is the standing answer to any who would go serve God, whether it is the three days' journey or keeping the Sabbath and the new moons now.
The officers did see that they were in evil case. That is when they realized no appeal to Pharaoh would deliver them; deliverance was not coming from Egypt.

They met Moses and Aaron and said, The LORD look upon you, and judge; because ye have made our savour to be abhorred in the eyes of Pharaoh, and in the eyes of his servants, to put a sword in their hand to slay us.

Moses returned unto the LORD, and said, Lord, wherefore hast thou so evil entreated this people? why is it that thou hast sent me? For since I came to Pharaoh to speak in thy name, he hath done evil to this people; neither hast thou delivered thy people at all.
